topic.name: ROS1
topic.short_description: Receptor tyrosine kinase fusion in lung cancer
topic.seo_title: ROS1 Fusion Cancer Research - Latest Studies & Findings | Your Cancer Breakthroughs
topic.seo_description: Explore ROS1 fusion in lung cancer research. Discover latest biomarker discoveries, diagnostic advances, and treatment breakthroughs from peer-reviewed studies.
topic.seo_intro:
ROS1 is a receptor tyrosine kinase that, when fused with other genes, drives the development of certain lung cancers. This fusion occurs when parts of the ROS1 gene abnormally join with another gene, creating a hybrid protein that signals cancer cells to grow uncontrollably. ROS1 fusions are found in approximately 1-2% of non-small cell lung cancers, making them a relatively rare but significant biomarker for diagnosis and treatment planning. Identifying ROS1 fusions has become increasingly important because patients with these mutations often respond well to targeted therapies designed specifically to inhibit this fusion protein, offering a personalized approach to cancer care.

Researchers continue to advance our understanding of ROS1-positive lung cancers through improved diagnostic methods and the development of new targeted drugs. Biomarker testing for ROS1 fusion helps oncologists quickly identify patients who may benefit from specific treatments, improving outcomes and reducing unnecessary side effects from broader chemotherapy approaches. Current research focuses on overcoming drug resistance, identifying patients who might benefit from combination therapies, and understanding which ROS1 fusion variants respond best to different treatments. This precision medicine approach represents a fundamental shift in how lung cancer is diagnosed and treated.

On this page, you'll find the latest peer-reviewed research articles on ROS1 fusion in lung cancer, including studies on diagnostic techniques, clinical trial results, and emerging therapeutic strategies. These resources represent the most current scientific findings to help patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers stay informed about ROS1-related cancer research and treatment innovations.

articles.title: Long-Term Efficacy and Safety of Taletrectinib in Patients With ROS1+ Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Results From the Phase II TRUST-I Study.
articles.summary: Taletrectinib shows durable long-term effectiveness in treating advanced ROS1-positive lung cancer, with response lasting over four years in treatment-naive patients.

articles.title: Stage IIIB ROS1-Positive NSCLC management: crizotinib + surgery + TCM achieves exceptionally prolonged PFS (a case report).
articles.summary: Combining targeted therapy, surgery, and traditional Chinese medicine extended lung cancer survival to 62 months versus typical 20 months.

articles.title: Expanded Access Treatment of Zidesamtinib (NVL-520) in Patients With Advanced ROS1+ NSCLC or Other ROS1+ Solid Tumors
articles.summary: The expanded access program allows ROS1+ cancer patients with limited treatment options to receive zidesamtinib, an investigational drug, outside of clinical trials.

articles.title: NCI-COG Pediatric MATCH (Molecular Analysis for Therapy Choice)- Phase 2 Subprotocol of Ensartinib in Patients With Tumors Harboring ALK or ROS1 Genomic Alterations
articles.summary: Ensartinib shows promise in treating pediatric solid tumors and lymphomas with ALK or ROS1 genetic alterations that have recurred or are treatment-resistant.

articles.title: Rapidly progressive arthropathy identified on imaging of patients treated with Crizotinib for ALK-rearranged/ROS1-positive non small cell lung cancer: A retrospective single-center study.
articles.summary: Researchers found that crizotinib treatment for ALK/ROS1-positive lung cancer patients can lead to unexpectedly rapid joint deterioration.
